stem:
The diagram shows Gopal's paper kite with a possible vertical mid-line drawn as a dashed fold line.

When is that mid-line a line of symmetry?

options.text: When folding along the mid-line makes the two parts overlap exactly point for point.
When the two halves look roughly similar from a distance.
Calling the mid-line a line of symmetry is what forces the two parts to match.
The mid-line is a line of symmetry for any paper kite, even when the fold test is never tried.

teacher.key_rationale: A line of symmetry requires the exact fold-overlap test. Rough similarity omits exact overlap. Saying the label forces the match reverses the relation. Claiming every kite mid-line is symmetric without the fold test over-extends the rule.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as a paper kite with a dashed vertical fold line.
